newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises 80 bps to 11.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises 80 bps to 11.1 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose 80 basis points to 11.1 percent on Friday, boosted by exceptionally strong demand ahead of the weekend.
The day's settlements totalled 55.8 million kuna, but demand ovrshot supply by almost as much -- 46.2 million kuna.
Fresh loans accounted for 36.8 million of the total.
Dealers said corporate tax payments and cash withdrawals earlier this week, because of the May 1 public holiday, left as many as 19 banks short of cash today.
The weighted call money rate rose to 10.6 from 10.3 percent as some creditors charged a higher 12 percent for new funds.
Interbank term rates were also firmer again at 12-17 percent after slight cuts earlier in the week.
Insurers rolled over their one-week and 10-day loans at a steady nine percent rate.
The central bank's kuna midrates firmed slightly to 6.1685 against the dollar, and eased to 3.5801 versus the German mark. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
